de23_design.topic: Urbit's address space: design, Yarvin's own descriptions, distribution and concentration

claims.text: Yarvin, 13 Jan 2010: any good namespace allocation must solve 'Zooko's triangle'; Urbit's quasi-solution is 'a design I call digital feudalism - of which more later'

2016 address-space post (Wolfe-Pauly and Yarvin): 256 galaxies allocated as of 1 June 2016: Tlon 95, urbit.org 50 (future foundation), Tlon employees and family 40 (24 to Yarvin, 16 to others), outside investors 34, 37 to 33 other individuals; 'If Bitcoin is money, Urbit is land'; 'digital land, not digital money'; ownership scattered so the system is 'unlikely to collapse back into a single landlord'; conventions: blocks split never merge, galaxies and stars owned by different parties, galaxies by individuals not corporations; admits Urbit 'does not live up to these ideals at present'; planets 32-bit, 'only 4 billion'

Interim Constitution (Tlon, 15 May 2016): consulate, galactic senate (galaxy holders, per galaxy, convenes to replace consuls, private), stellar congress, planetary assembly; 'For the interim, full authority is held by the (Roman style) consulate'; consulate effectively Tlon; Tlon's stated intent to eventually 'surrender governance of Urbit to its users'; document 'may be updated arbitrarily'

'Common Objections to Urbit' (2016): 'Curtis invented Urbit. So by the homestead principle, he started out owning all of it'; distribution 'looks a lot like land ownership in the real world'; 'Urbit is designed to govern itself collectively by address space ownership', effectively 'proof of stake'; 'When it's impossible to eliminate centralized power, it becomes necessary to tame, stabilize, and limit it'; long run every galaxy should have a separate human owner; gives Yarvin 20 galaxies (about 8%)

Urbit 2020: 'If Bitcoin is money and smart contracts are law, Urbit ID is land'; 'a self-authenticating property title'; 'Urbit IDs are scarce in order to discourage spam and abuse'; all address space was once owned by Curtis; 'Tlon bought half the address space from Curtis'

Yarvin, 'A Founder's Farewell', 13 Jan 2019: 'From the very start, I knew Urbit could not succeed until it ceased to be mine and became the world's'; resigned as CTO, board member and voting shareholder of Tlon; reassigned his personal galaxies to urbit.org (in Tlon's custody); kept a few thousand stars in long timelocks and a nonvoting minority stake; said these confer no power
Galactic Senate: voting is a power of galaxies; two proposal types, upgrade and document; quorum 64 galaxies (a quarter); absolute majority 129; vote ends at 30 days or on absolute majority

Smith and Burrows (2021): about 4 billion planets, 65,280 stars and 256 galaxies; per Tseng (2019) Tlon ~37%, urbit.org 19%, Tlon employees 15%, outside investors 13%, donors/contributors 14%; earlier versions used 'Lords', 'Dukes' and 'Earls' derived from Lockean homesteading (Lecher, Verge 2017); Urbit 'necessarily governed by a technocratic elite of stars and galaxies'; 'the only liberty is exit'

The Point (9 Sept 2022): Urbit's 2010 whitepaper titled a section on address-space allocation 'digital feudalism'; 'a bare-bones messaging server, with, at most, a few thousand active users'; a star about $6,000 on the open market; galaxy = 1/256 of address space; backed by Thiel and a16z

Astra (13 Oct 2022): Lehman on whether the hierarchy is 'digital feudalism': 'No. Facebook is digital feudalism. When you don't have explicit hierarchies, it's way worse.'; galaxies traded privately at values 'reaching over one million U.S. dollars'

Compact (18 June 2025): per Tseng, as of 2019 185 of 256 galaxies owned by Tlon, Tlon employees and Urbit Foundation employees, and almost 38,000 of 65,500 stars; 'address space ownership is highly concentrated'; Yarvin designed decision-making power proportional to address-space ownership and 'has called Urbit a "transparent plutocracy"'; he holds 'in his own words' the position of 'the prince'
CoinDesk (10 May 2023): about 90 monthly active developers; ships 'roughly doubled this year'; Urbit Foundation split off from Tlon in 2021

Tlon FAQ: Tlon builds Tlon Messenger on the Urbit stack and offers hosting; on sign-up Tlon generates the identity and 'We custody the wallet for you, but it is yours'; identity is a cryptographic proof on Ethereum; Tlon created 2013, created the Urbit Foundation in 2021
Compact (2025): Yarvin described the 2024 crisis as 'controlled flight into terrain'; the Foundation 'admitted that it had run out of capital'; developers were paid in address space
~sorreg-namtyv is Curtis Yarvin's Urbit identity (byline of 'A Founder's Farewell' and co-author of 'The Urbit Address Space')

Urbit blog posts Nov 2025-May 2026 by the Foundation and contributors: vere64 runtime preview, LLM tooling, 'Sovereign Intelligence' by ~sicdev-pilnup (13 Jan 2026), 'This Month in Urbit: April 2026' (1 May 2026); none report user counts

'A Founder's Farewell' (13 Jan 2019): Yarvin said he would no longer contribute code or write or speak publicly about Urbit; 'The soil in which these flowers grow must be level and neutral'; Urbit 'a decentralized network of social networks'

Urbit blog index: 'Azimuth is On-Chain' (13 Jan 2019): 'The Urbit address space, now called Azimuth, is on the blockchain'; 'Azimuth's First Contract Upgrade' (4 June 2021), subtitled 'Galactic Senate makes first concrete action' (audit re-check 28 Oct 2026)

de23_return.topic: Yarvin's 2024 return, the 2025 board fight, the Galactic Senate's board, funding, status October 2026; Book IV close

claims.text: CoinDesk 21 Aug 2024: the Urbit Foundation board sacked Josh Lehman, executive director since 2021, and named Christopher Colby interim; CTO Ted Blackman and engineer Liam Fitzgerald left; Yarvin: 'Josh is an excellent peacetime CEO'; 'For that, you need a wartime CEO'; 'We're here to fix this'; he holds no formal position but will lead strategy; runway 'measurable in months'; foundation to retain 50% of staff; Lehman's Ethereum layer-2 plan scrapped; utility token possibly on Base considered; star price fell from about $27,000 (late 2021) to a little over $1,000

Marbl (6 July 2025): four executive directors in a year; Kneer at the helm eight months; Kneer and Yarvin joined forces November 2024; Kneer fired Yarvin from the board the previous week; Yarvin lobbied the other two board members to fire Kneer; Kneer called a no-confidence vote and asked galaxy holders to replace the board; at writing 19 votes, 18 for and 1 against; author knows Kneer for a decade and urged a yes vote

Rettig (27 July 2025): Yarvin 'Executive Director-by-fiat'; 'real Roman times'; Foundation ran out of money the year before; most staff quit; a16z invested $4M for more address space (terms unknown); galactic vote expected, outcome not reported; author owns some address space

Urbit Foundation, 9 Oct 2025: 'The Galactic Senate has elected to replace the board of the Urbit Foundation' after 'multiple votes'; new three-seat board ~lavlyn-litmeg, ~palfun-foslup, ~hocfur-modlex; board appoints ~sicdev-pilnup executive director, succeeding ~sorreg-namtyv, 'who is leaving to found a new application development company'; Foundation 'struggled during periods of uncertainty around both funding and leadership'; outside capital from venture capitalists and Bitcoin philanthropists

Kofman (New Yorker, June 2025): after decades and an estimated $30 million, Urbit resembles Usenet more than a feudal society; in the initial design Yarvin named himself 'prince'; returned last year as 'wartime CEO' after several key employees resigned; sought a16z money again in February; unpublished Substack draft: plan to promote Urbit as an elite private club whose members would be stars of 'a new Usenet, a new digital Athens'
Empire podcast description (24 Sept 2024): Yarvin presents Urbit as a fix for centralised 'social databases', discussing digital sovereignty and 'accountable monarchies' in digital governance

Rio Times (17 Aug 2026): Honduras Prospera Inc. v. Honduras, ICSID ARB/23/2, initially US$10.775bn, reported trimmed to ~US$1.63bn in 2025, undecided; Congress repealed the ZEDE law April 2022; Supreme Court ruled ZEDE decrees unconstitutional 20 Sept 2024; Honduras rejoined ICSID 16 Aug 2026 under Asfura
PolitiFact (Feb 2026, modified July 2026): Trump's 2023 pledge of 10 freedom cities on federal land rated Stalled; no bill on Congress.gov, no executive order or federal land action found
